title: 267. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Rational Function Removable Discontinuities
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a removable discontinuity in a rational function.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=\frac{(x-2)(x+3)}{x-2}\), what type of discontinuity does the graph have at \(x=2\)?
questions.explanation: The factor \(x-2\) appears in both the numerator and the denominator, so it cancels. The simplified function is \(x+3\) for \(x\ne2\). Since the canceled factor makes the original denominator zero at \(x=2\), the graph has a hole there. Therefore the discontinuity is removable, so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Cancel common factors before deciding whether a discontinuity is removable.

questions.concept: Locating a Hole in a Rational Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the coordinates of a removable discontinuity.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=\frac{(x-1)(x+4)}{x-1}\) has a hole at which point?
questions.explanation: Cancel the common factor \(x-1\). The simplified function is \(x+4\) for \(x\ne1\). At \(x=1\), the \(y\)-value of the hole is \(1+4=5\). Therefore the hole is at \((1,5)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: After canceling the common factor, substitute the excluded \(x\)-value into the simplified expression.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the \(x\)-value of a removable discontinuity by factoring.
questions.question: What is the \(x\)-value of the removable discontinuity of \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}\)?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator: \(x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2)\). Then \(f(x)=\frac{(x-2)(x+2)}{x-2}\). The factor \(x-2\) cancels, so \(x=2\) is a hole. Therefore the removable discontinuity occurs at \(x=2\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Factor the numerator and look for a common factor with the denominator.

questions.concept: Identifying a Function with a Removable Discontinuity
questions.learningObjective: Select the rational function that has a removable discontinuity at a given \(x\)-value.
questions.question: Which function has a removable discontinuity at \(x=3\)?
questions.explanation: In \(f(x)=\frac{(x-3)(x+1)}{x-3}\), the factor \(x-3\) cancels, so \(x=3\) is a hole. In \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x-3}\), the factor \(x-3\) does not cancel, so \(x=3\) is a vertical asymptote. Therefore option A is correct.
questions.hint: A removable discontinuity occurs when a common factor cancels.

questions.concept: Coordinates of a Hole after Cancellation
questions.learningObjective: Determine the coordinates of a removable discontinuity after simplifying.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}\) has a hole at which point?
questions.explanation: Factor the numerator: \(x^2-9=(x-3)(x+3)\). Cancel \(x-3\), so \(f(x)=x+3\) for \(x\ne3\). At \(x=3\), the \(y\)-value of the hole is \(3+3=6\). Therefore the hole is at \((3,6)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Substitute the excluded \(x\)-value into the simplified expression to find the hole's \(y\)-coordinate.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the simplified function and the hole of a rational function.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=\frac{(x+1)(x-2)}{x+1}\), which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: It simplifies to \(y=x-2\) with a hole at \((-1,-3)\).

options.label: B
options.text: It simplifies to \(y=x+1\) with a hole at \((-1,0)\).

questions.explanation: Cancel the common factor \(x+1\). The simplified function is \(y=x-2\) for \(x\ne-1\). At \(x=-1\), the \(y\)-value of the hole is \(-1-2=-3\). Therefore the function simplifies to \(y=x-2\) with a hole at \((-1,-3)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Cancel the common factor first, then evaluate the simplified function at the excluded \(x\)-value.

questions.concept: Identifying a Function with a Hole
questions.learningObjective: Select the rational function that has a removable discontinuity at a specified point.
questions.question: Which rational function has a hole at \(x=-2\)?
questions.explanation: In \(f(x)=\frac{(x+2)(x-1)}{x+2}\), the factor \(x+2\) cancels, so \(x=-2\) is a hole. In \(f(x)=\frac{1}{x+2}\), the denominator factor \(x+2\) does not cancel, so \(x=-2\) is a vertical asymptote. Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: A hole occurs when the factor causing the zero in the denominator also appears in the numerator.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which discontinuities are removable and which are vertical asymptotes.
questions.question: For \(f(x)=\frac{x+3}{x^2+5x+6}\), which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: \(x=-3\) is a vertical asymptote, and \(x=-2\) is a hole.

options.label: B
options.text: \(x=-3\) is a hole, and \(x=-2\) is a vertical asymptote.

questions.explanation: Factor the denominator: \(x^2+5x+6=(x+3)(x+2)\). The factor \(x+3\) cancels with the numerator, so \(x=-3\) is a hole. The remaining denominator factor \(x+2\) gives a vertical asymptote at \(x=-2\). Therefore option B is correct.
questions.hint: Cancel common factors first; the remaining denominator factors determine vertical asymptotes.

questions.concept: Coordinates of a Hole from a Rational Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine the coordinates of a removable discontinuity after factoring.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x^2-3x+2}\) has a hole at which point?
questions.explanation:
Factor numerator and denominator:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2-1 &= (x-1)(x+1)\\
x^2-3x+2 &= (x-1)(x-2)
\end{aligned}
\]
Cancel \(x-1\), so \(f(x)=\frac{x+1}{x-2}\) for \(x\ne1\). At \(x=1\), the \(y\)-value of the hole is \(\frac{1+1}{1-2}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2\). Therefore the hole is at \((1,-2)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Factor completely, cancel the common factor, then substitute the excluded \(x\)-value into the simplified expression.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the coordinates of a hole by fully simplifying a rational function.
questions.question: The graph of \(f(x)=\frac{x^2-5x+6}{x^2-4x+3}\) has a hole at which point?
questions.explanation:
Factor numerator and denominator:
\[
\begin{aligned}
x^2-5x+6 &= (x-2)(x-3)\\
x^2-4x+3 &= (x-1)(x-3)
\end{aligned}
\]
Cancel \(x-3\), so \(f(x)=\frac{x-2}{x-1}\) for \(x\ne3\). At \(x=3\), the \(y\)-value of the hole is \(\frac{3-2}{3-1}=\frac{1}{2}\). Therefore the hole is at \(\left(3,\frac{1}{2}\right)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Factor both numerator and denominator, cancel the common factor, then evaluate at the excluded \(x\)-value.
